claims.text: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Kyiv for the first time since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner travelled to Kyiv by train due to the risk of Russian drone strikes.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky greeted Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner at Kyiv's Saint Sophia Cathedral.
Russian drones hit the headquarters of Ukraine's security services near Saint Sophia Cathedral on Friday.
UK National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell and other European national security advisers joined the talks in Kyiv.
Vladimir Putin told US envoys in Moscow that Russia was making 'tangible advances' on the battlefield.
Ukrainian officials claim that in August Russia suffered 42,000 dead or wounded casualties and Ukraine gained more territory than it lost.
Russia and Ukraine agreed to a short-term pause in air strikes during the US envoys' visit to Kyiv.
Russian strikes bombed Kyiv's two main airports on Friday, forcing Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff to travel by train.
Russia and Ukraine pledged to refrain from attacking each other's capitals over the weekend to ensure safe passage for the US envoys.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine is counting on a winter package from the US and Europe including air defence, energy support, and American LNG.
Ukrainian authorities reported on Sunday that at least eight people were killed and 69 injured across Ukraine in the past day.
Peace talks between Russia and Ukraine have focused on a 20-point peace plan put forward by Washington and Kyiv in December.
US envoy Steve Witkoff stated that peace talks in Ukraine have been 'very meaningful'.
Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held three hours of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday.
Ukraine reported striking the Ryazan oil refinery about 480 km inside Russia overnight, causing a fire.
At least five people were killed and five injured after an Amazon cargo plane overshot the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday and crashed into several vehicles.
Miami Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz stated there was 'no apparent threat to public safety' following the crash.
An Amazon cargo plane arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico, overshot the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday afternoon and struck several vehicles.
Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava stated that five people were killed and five others were injured in the crash.
The FAA confirmed 21 Air Flight 7598, a Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft, overran the runway at Miami International Airport around 2 pm local time on Sunday, September 6.
All runways and taxiways at Miami International Airport were closed as of 3 pm following the cargo plane crash.
More than 60 units from Miami-Dade Fire Rescue responded to the scene of the plane crash.
Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office closed NW 67th Avenue between NW 25th Street and NW 36th Street following the crash.
US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy stated that the agency issued a full ground stop in Miami after the crash.
The Boeing 767-300 cargo plane involved in the crash was over 32 years old, having first flown in June 1994 as a passenger aircraft.
Cargo carrier 21 Air began operating Boeing 767-300 freighters for Amazon in 2024.
Incomplete results show Alternative for Germany (AfD) set to win a record 44% of the vote in the Saxony-Anhalt state election.
AfD state leader Ulrich Siegmund described the election result in Saxony-Anhalt as 'sensational'.
Saxony-Anhalt has a population of 2.1 million and its branch of the AfD is classified by domestic intelligence as 'right-wing extremist'.
Voter turnout in the Saxony-Anhalt state election was estimated at 78%.
The conservative CDU finished second in the Saxony-Anhalt election with just over 17% of the vote.
Exit polls showed Die Linke won 9.3%, the Social Democrats won 8.4%, and the Greens won 8.7% in the Saxony-Anhalt state election.
The BSW party reached the 5% threshold required to enter the state parliament in Saxony-Anhalt.
AfD candidate Ulrich Siegmund promised to launch a remigration and deportation offensive, ban rainbow flags in schools, and halt new windfarm construction if AfD forms a government.
Modern Germany has never had a far-right or right-wing populist party lead a national government, state government, or major-city administration since World War II.
CDU national general secretary Franziska Hoppermann described the election result as 'very difficult' for her party while rejecting cooperation with the AfD.
The US denied Iran's claim that it struck an unmanned American vessel near the Strait of Hormuz, calling the allegation a 'total lie'.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated on CNN that around 9 million barrels of oil a day were currently passing through the Strait of Hormuz.
The US-Iran conflict began on February 28 with US and Israeli attacks on Iran.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated on ABC that there 'may not' be a nuclear agreement reached with Iran.
According to a New York Times report, August was the deadliest month for merchant vessels in the Strait of Hormuz area since March.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that Americans must understand 'before it is too late' that the 'rules of the game have changed'.
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth warned that if Iran shoots at US ships, the US will destroy and sink their oil tankers.
The average price for one gallon of diesel in the US reached $5.85 on Friday.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated that the US is degrading Iran's capacity to develop nuclear weapons and deliver them.
Two new eruptions were recorded as Indonesia's Anak Krakatau continued to spew volcanic ash, disrupting hundreds of flights across six airports.
Indonesian authorities temporarily suspended operations at eight airports due to volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau, leaving around 170,000 passengers stranded.
The Indonesian transport ministry reported that 1,558 flights were delayed due to airport closures.
Volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau reached up to 20,000 feet on the Java side and 50,000 feet on the Sumatra side.
Indonesian authorities confirmed there is no tsunami warning associated with the recent activity of Anak Krakatau.
Booming sounds from the eruption of Anak Krakatau were heard up to 435 miles (700 km) away.
Indonesia's disaster mitigation agency BNPB announced plans to conduct a weather modification operation involving cloud-seeding to wash away volcanic ash.
Port authorities prohibited ships in the Sunda Strait from going within a two-mile radius of Anak Krakatau.
Volcanic ash from Mount Anak Krakatau forced the suspension of over 300 flights at Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on Sunday.
A previous eruption and collapse of Anak Krakatau in 2018 triggered a tsunami that killed over 400 people.
